extracted.intended_audience: researchers and practitioners working on LLM evaluation, dataset/benchmark creators, and ML/AI researchers interested in mathematical reasoning for language models
extracted.subtask_description: Designing and evaluating automated, scalable benchmarks that probe chain-of-thought mathematical reasoning in large language models by logically chaining problems (forward and backward) and measuring model performance as chain complexity increases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benchmark must capture model reasoning differentials
rubrics_metrics.description: Existing widely-used benchmarks such as GSM8K marginally encapsulate model reasoning differentials - most state-of-the-art models for example achieve over 94% accuracy on the GSM8K dataset (paperwithcode, 2024).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A good benchmark should expose differences in reasoning ability among top models rather than saturating; avoid datasets where SOTA models cluster near ceiling performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benchmarks should be automated and scalable
rubrics_metrics.description: While constructing harder benchmarks is possible, their creation is often manual, expensive, and unscalable. As such, we present Scheherazade, an automated approach to produce large quantities of challenging mathematical reasoning benchmarks by logically chaining a small starting set of problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer methods that can generate many examples from a small seed set without manual authoring, enabling repeatable, large-scale evaluations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use logical chaining to increase problem complexity
rubrics_metrics.description: Produce challenging mathematical reasoning benchmarks by logically chaining a small starting set of problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chaining should create multi-step dependencies so solving later problems requires reasoning across earlier linked problems; chains should increase the cognitive load required versus independent problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support both forward chaining and backward chaining
rubrics_metrics.description: We propose two different chaining methods, forward chaining and backward chaining.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Benchmark generators should implement multiple chaining paradigms (e.g., forward where solutions feed into later problems, and backward where target facts are decomposed), since models may perform differently under each.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduce randomized branching to create combinatorial complexity
rubrics_metrics.description: Which include randomized branching techniques to generate complex reasoning problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate random branching during chaining to create diverse tree-like problem structures and avoid deterministic predictable patterns; this increases difficulty and variety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure performance as chain length / complexity increases
rubrics_metrics.description: We show that while other frontier models' performance declines precipitously at only a few questions chained, our evaluation suggests o1-preview's performance persists, with the flagship OpenAI model the only one to perform better at backward reasoning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate models across varying chain lengths and structural complexities to observe how robustness degrades; report trends (e.g., accuracy vs chain length) rather than single-point results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use established datasets as seeds and report comparative metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: We apply Scheherazade on GSM8K to create GSM8K-Scheherazade and evaluate 3 frontier LLMs and OpenAI's o1-preview on it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Build on familiar benchmarks so results are comparable; report standard metrics (e.g., accuracy) and compare multiple models, highlighting differences in forward vs backward reasoning performance.
